record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.context_brief: compact CDH spaces without Cantor sets
record.original_question: Does there exist a compact countable dense homogeneous space that contains no copy of the Cantor set?

evidence.quote: Problem 31. Is there a compact CDH-space which does not contain a copy of the Cantor set?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological space $X$ is called countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if $X$ is separable and, for every pair of countable dense subsets $D_1, D_2 \subseteq X$, there exists a homeomorphism $h \colon X \to X$ with $h(D_1) = D_2$. A space is said to contain a copy of the Cantor set if it has a subspace homeomorphic to the standard Cantor set $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$.

Question: Does there exist a compact Hausdorff space that is countable dense homogeneous and contains no topological copy of the Cantor set?
artifact.status_search_result: Under the Continuum Hypothesis, a compact Hausdorff CDH crowded space containing no copy of the Cantor set has been constructed (Hrušák, "Countable dense homogeneity and the Cantor set", arXiv:1705.01203). A ZFC construction does not appear to be known, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Countable dense homogeneity and the Cantor set
status_evidence.snippet: Assuming CH, there exists a compact Hausdorff space that is countable dense homogeneous, crowded and does not contain topological copies of the Cantor set.
status_evidence.claim: A consistent positive answer is known under CH.
